Pure string/path logic —\n113\t/// no environment reads, no filesystem canonicalization, no `current_exe`.\n114\t/// `dir` is a parameter (rather than derived from the process) so this is\n115\t/// independently unit-testable with crafted PATH literals.\n116\t///\n117\t/// This is the self-recursion guard's filter: the future resolve_real_binary\n118\t/// (bf-614q) strips the shim dir ([`shim_dir`]) from PATH so the real-cargo\n119\t/// lookup cannot re-resolve `cargo` to the gantry shim itself (plan §1\n120\t/// \"Real-binary resolution\"). `dir` is compared as a [`std::path::Path`], so\n121\t/// trailing-slash and `.`-component variants of the same directory match.\n122\t///\n123\t/// Separator hygiene: the filter only *removes* entries, so re-joining the\n124\t/// survivors can never introduce a spurious empty (CWD) entry — no leading,\n125\t/// double, or trailing separator appears that was not already implied by the\n126\t/// input. Existing empty entries already present in `path_var` are preserved\n127\t/// (the \"dir absent → effectively unchanged\" guarantee): an empty entry is not\n128\t/// `dir`, so it survives untouched.\n129\t//\n130\t// Held private by design (a resolve_real_binary-internal helper, like\n131\t// shim_dir): only resolve_real_binary is meant to call it.\n132\tfn strip_dir_from_path(path_var: &str, dir: &std::path::Path) -> String {\n133\t    // `split` on a single separator yields one substring per PATH entry, with\n134\t    // empty entries (leading/double/trailing separators) preserved as \"\" —\n135\t    // which re-join back to the original separator shape. Comparing each entry\n136\t    // as a Path (rather than a raw string) makes `/b` match a `/b/` or\n137\t    // `/x/./b`-style entry without canonicalizing anything on disk.\n138\t    path_var\n139\t        .split(PATH_SEP)\n140\t        .filter(|entry| std::path::Path::new(*entry) != dir)\n141\t        .collect::<Vec<&str>>()\n142\t        .join(PATH_SEP)\n143\t}\n144\t\n145\t/// Find an executable named `name` by walking `path` left to right.\n146\t///\n147\t/// Splits `path` on the OS PATH separator ([`PATH_SEP`]) and, for each entry in\n148\t/// order, checks whether `<entry>/<name>` is an existing executable regular\n149\t/// file. Returns [`Ok`] with the first matching path — PATH order respected —\n150\t/// or [`Err`] naming `name` if no entry matches. A pure lookup over a\n151\t/// caller-supplied PATH string: no environment read of its own and no\n152\t/// `current_exe`. The caller is responsible for stripping gantry's own shim dir\n153\t/// ([`shim_dir`] via [`strip_dir_from_path`]) first, so the lookup cannot\n154\t/// re-resolve `cargo` to the gantry shim itself (plan §1 \"Real-binary\n155\t/// resolution\").\n156\t///\n157\t/// Non-existent entries, directories, and non-executable or non-regular files\n158\t/// are skipped silently: a stale or misconfigured PATH slot is a skip, not a\n159\t/// failure. Only the total absence of a match is an error, and the message\n160\t/// always names `name` so a missing-real-cargo diagnostic is actionable — this\n161\t/// helper never silently falls back to a default binary.\n162\t///\n163\t/// Never panics. A filesystem error on a given candidate (the directory gone,\n164\t/// a permission-denied stat) surfaces as \"not a match\" for that entry and the\n165\t/// walk continues, because one bad PATH slot must not abort the whole lookup.\n166\t//\n167\t// Held private by design (a resolve_real_binary-internal helper, like\n168\t// shim_dir and strip_dir_from_path): only resolve_real_binary is meant to\n169\t// call it.\n170\tfn find_in_path(name: &str, path: &str) -> Result<std::path::PathBuf, String> {\n171\t    for entry in path.split(PATH_SEP) {\n172\t        let candidate = std::path::Path::new(entry).join(name);\n173\t        if is_executable_file(&candidate) {\n174\t            return Ok(candidate);\n175\t        }\n176\t    }\n177\t    Err(format!(\n178\t        \"gantry could not find `{name}` on PATH; install the real binary or set `real_binary` in config\"\n179\t    ))\n180\t}\n181\t\n182\t/// Whether `candidate` is an existing executable regular file.\n183\t///\n184\t/// `std::fs::metadata` (not `symlink_metadata`) follows a symlink to its\n185\t/// target, so a PATH entry pointing at a symlinked binary resolves correctly;\n186\t/// a broken symlink, a missing file, a directory, or any non-regular entry is a\n187\t/// non-match rather than an error — a stat failure is a skip for [`find_in_path`].\n188\t/// The platform-specific notion of \"executable\" is delegated to\n189\t/// [`is_executable`].\n190\tfn is_executable_file(candidate: &std::path::Path) -> bool {\n191\t    let Ok(md) = std::fs::metadata(candidate) else {\n192\t        return false;\n193\t    };\n194\t    md.is_file() && is_executable(candidate, &md)\n195\t}\n196\t\n197\t/// Whether a regular file is executable.\n198\t///\n199\t/// Platform-specific because the notion differs: Unix consults the mode bits\n200\t/// carried in [`std::fs::Metadata`]; Windows carries no execute bit and infers\n201\t/// runnability from the file extension. Reads no environment (no `PATHEXT`) —\n202\t/// the conventional executable extensions are fixed here so this helper honors\n203\t/// the \"no env reads of its own\" contract shared with [`find_in_path`].\n204\t#[cfg(unix)]\n205\tfn is_executable(_candidate: &std::path::Path, md: &std::fs::Metadata) -> bool {\n206\t    use std::os::unix::fs::PermissionsExt;\n207\t    // Any execute bit (user/group/other) qualifies — matching shell PATH\n208\t    // lookup, which treats a file runnable by anyone as found.\n209\t    md.permissions().mode() & 0o111 != 0\n210\t}\n211\t\n212\t#[cfg(windows)]\n213\tfn is_executable(candidate: &std::path::Path, _md: &std::fs::Metadata) -> bool {\n214\t    // No execute bit exists on Windows; runnability is conventionally a\n215\t    // property of the extension. A PATHEXT env read would violate the helper's\n216\t    // \"no env reads of its own\" contract, so the common executable extensions\n217\t    // are matched directly.\n218\t    matches!(\n219\t        candidate.extension().and_then(|e| e.to_str()),\n220\t        Some(\"exe\") | Some(\"bat\") | Some(\"cmd\") | Some(\"com\")\n221\t    )\n222\t}\n223\t\n224\t/// Resolve the real `cargo` binary the shim should hand off to (plan §1\n225\t/// \"Real-binary resolution\", Components §1 \"Shim & dispatcher\").\n226\t///\n227\t/// Composes the three private helpers into the top-level resolution path the\n228\t/// dispatcher consults before any pipeline stage runs:\n229\t///\n230\t/// 1. **Override short-circuit** — when\n231\t///    [`crate::config::Config::real_binary`] is `Some`, return that path\n232\t///    verbatim with *no* PATH search. The explicit override is trusted as-is\n233\t///    (it need not exist on disk; exec-check is a later stage's concern), so a\n234\t///    pinned toolchain is honored without touching the environment.\n235\t/// 2. **PATH lookup** — otherwise, derive gantry's own binary dir ([`shim_dir`]),\n236\t///    strip it from `PATH` ([`strip_dir_from_path`]) so the walk cannot\n237\t///    re-resolve `cargo` to the gantry shim itself (the self-recursion guard,\n238\t///    enforced here at the resolution layer), then walk the survivors\n239\t///    left-to-right for `cargo` ([`find_in_path`]).\n240\t///\n241\t/// Never silently falls through to the gantry binary or to `None`: a missing\n242\t/// `cargo` on the stripped PATH propagates [`find_in_path`]'s `Err` verbatim, so\n243\t/// a broken install surfaces as a diagnostic instead of an infinite re-exec.\n244\t/// Never panics — every fallible step maps to a human-readable `Err`. Spawns no\n245\t/// process and consults no other gantry pipeline module (gate/refs/backend/\n246\t/// local/runlog): this is decision-only resolution.\n247\t///\n248\t/// This is the integration seam the bf-614q chain lands. [`shim_dir`],\n249\t/// [`strip_dir_from_path`], and [`find_in_path`] each shipped standalone in\n250\t/// earlier children; `resolve_real_binary` is their first and only caller, which\n251\t/// is why their provisional `#[allow(dead_code)]` attributes retired at this\n252\t/// commit.\n253\tpub fn resolve_real_binary(cfg: &crate::config::Config) -> Result<std::path::PathBuf, String> {\n254\t    // 1. Explicit override: trust it verbatim and skip the PATH search entirely.\n255\t    if let Some(path) = &cfg.real_binary {\n256\t        return Ok(path.clone());\n257\t    }\n258\t\n259\t    // 2. Exclude gantry's own binary dir so the lookup cannot re-resolve\n260\t    //    `cargo` to the gantry shim (self-recursion guard), then walk the\n261\t    //    surviving PATH entries left-to-right for `cargo`.\n262\t    let shim = shim_dir()?;\n263\t    let path_var = std::env::var(\"PATH\")\n264\t        .map_err(|e| format!(\"gantry cannot read the PATH environment variable: {e}\"))?;\n265\t    let stripped = strip_dir_from_path(&path_var, &shim);\n266\t    find_in_path(\"cargo\", &stripped)\n267\t}\n268\t\n269\t#[cfg(test)]\n270\tmod tests {\n271\t    use super::*;\n272\t    use crate::config::Config;\n273\t    use std::sync::Mutex;\n274\t\n275\t    #[test]\n276\t    fn strips_directory_to_basename() {\n277\t        // The load-bearing case: the shim sits ahead of the real toolchain\n278\t        // under a full path, but dispatch keys on the bare name.\n279\t        assert_eq!(\n280\t            invocation_name(&[\"/home/u/.local/bin/cargo\".to_string()]),\n281\t            \"cargo\"\n282\t        );\n283\t    }\n284\t\n285\t    #[test]\n286\t    fn bare_names_pass_through_unchanged() {\n287\t        assert_eq!(invocation_name(&[\"cargo\".to_string()]), \"cargo\");\n288\t        assert_eq!(invocation_name(&[\"gantry\".to_string()]), \"gantry\");\n289\t    }\n290\t\n291\t    #[test]\n292\t    fn relative_path_basename_is_taken() {\n293\t        assert_eq!(invocation_name(&[\"./cargo\".to_string()]), \"cargo\");\n294\t        assert_eq!(invocation_name(&[\"bin/cargo\".to_string()]), \"cargo\");\n295\t    }\n296\t\n297\t    #[test]\n298\t    fn unknown_name_is_returned_verbatim() {\n299\t        // main.rs's `other` arm matches whatever falls through; This file holds the no-I/O, decision-only pieces of the shim\n// that main.rs consults *before* any pipeline stage runs. It is deliberately a\n// self-contained leaf: it touches no filesystem, spawns no process, and\n// references no other gantry module (gate/refs/backend/local/runlog), so it\n// compiles and unit-tests standalone ahead of the rest of the skeleton wiring\n// (bf-2w7).\n//\n// `invocation_name` lives here because argv[0] is the dispatch key main.rs\n// matches on ('cargo' vs 'gantry' vs unknown). Real-binary resolution and the\n// passthrough exec join it here across the bf-614q chain: `shim_dir` is the\n// first piece (the self-recursion-guard basis), and resolve_real_binary\n// (bf-614q) composes it with the PATH lookup; the re-exec guard (bf-1m69) and\n// passthrough (bf-28dv) follow.\n\n/// The sentinel dispatch key returned when argv[0] is absent or basename-less.\n///\n/// Chosen so a degenerate invocation routes to the management CLI\n/// (`gantry version` / `gantry help`) rather than silently treating a broken\n/// argv[0] as a cargo offload, and so the fallback is a constant main.rs can\n/// match against without parsing.\nconst SENTINEL: &str = \"gantry\";\n\n/// The dispatch key derived from `argv[0]`: the basename of how the binary was\n/// invoked, with any directory component stripped.\n///\n/// main.rs matches the result to pick a profile — `cargo` selects the cargo\n/// tool profile (which may offload an intercepted subcommand), `gantry` selects\n/// the management CLI, and anything else falls through to the cargo profile as\n/// the safe default (plan §1).\n///\n/// `/home/u/.local/bin/cargo` → `cargo`; `cargo` → `cargo`; `gantry` → `gantry`.\n///\n/// Never panics. An empty `argv`, an `argv[0]` with no basename (e.g. `\"\"`,\n/// `\".\"`, `\"..\"`, a bare `\"/\"`), or a path that ends in a separator all yield\n/// the stable sentinel [`SENTINEL`] — dispatch then lands on the management CLI\n/// instead of indexing into a hole.\npub fn invocation_name(argv: &[String]) -> String {\n    // An absent argv[0] (empty argv) carries no invocation name; route to the\n    // management CLI deterministically rather than indexing into a hole.\n    let Some(argv0) = argv.first() else {\n        return SENTINEL.to_string();\n    };\n\n    // `Path::file_name` is the basename of argv[0] with every directory\n    // component stripped, in pure path logic (no filesystem access). It returns\n    // `None` for the empty string, `.` and `..`, and a lone root — exactly the\n    // shapes that carry no usable dispatch key. `to_str` never fails here\n    // because argv0 is already a UTF-8 `String`, but is kept for type hygiene.\n    match std::path::Path::new(argv0)\n        .file_name()\n        .and_then(|name| name.to_str())\n    {\n        Some(name) if !name.is_empty() => name.to_string(),\n        // basename-less argv[0] (including a trailing-slash-only path): fall to\n        // the sentinel so dispatch stays deterministic and panic-free.\n        _ => SENTINEL.to_string(),\n    }\n}\n\n/// The directory gantry must strip from PATH before resolving the real cargo —\n/// namely the directory that holds the gantry binary itself.\n///\n/// Returns the *parent* of `std::env::current_exe()`: a PATH entry pointing\n/// here would re-resolve `cargo` to the gantry shim, so this strip is the\n/// self-recursion guard's basis (plan §1 \"Real-binary resolution\"). Pure path\n/// logic — no PATH split, no cargo lookup, no filesystem stat beyond\n/// `current_exe()`, and no reference to Config; the future resolve_real_binary\n/// (bf-614q) consumes this to build the stripped search path.\n///\n/// Never panics. `current_exe()` can fail (platform path-resolution limits, a\n/// binary deleted mid-run, `/proc` unavailable on Linux); the failure surfaces\n/// as a human-readable `Err` rather than a panic or `unwrap`. On success the\n/// parent directory is returned — a directory path, never the binary file.\n//\n// Held private by design (the bead scope says \"private helper\"): only\n// resolve_real_binary is meant to call it.\nfn shim_dir() -> Result<std::path::PathBuf, String> {\n    let exe =\n        std::env::current_exe().map_err(|e| format!(\"gantry cannot locate its own binary: {e}\"))?;\n    // `parent()` is None only for a path with no directory component (a bare\n    // filename). `current_exe()` always carries a directory on supported\n    // platforms, so this is a defensive fallback surfaced as an error rather\n    // than an unwrap that could panic on an exotic shape.\n    exe.parent().map(std::path::PathBuf::from).ok_or_else(|| {\n        format!(\n            \"gantry binary path has no parent directory: {}\",\n            exe.display()\n        )\n    })\n}\n\n/// The character that separates entries in a PATH-style environment variable.\n///\n/// `:` on Unix-family targets, `;` on Windows. Pure string/path logic —\n/// no environment reads, no filesystem canonicalization, no `current_exe`.\n/// `dir` is a parameter (rather than derived from the process) so this is\n/// independently unit-testable with crafted PATH literals.\n///\n/// This is the self-recursion guard's filter: the future resolve_real_binary\n/// (bf-614q) strips the shim dir ([`shim_dir`]) from PATH so the real-cargo\n/// lookup cannot re-resolve `cargo` to the gantry shim itself (plan §1\n/// \"Real-binary resolution\"). `dir` is compared as a [`std::path::Path`], so\n/// trailing-slash and `.`-component variants of the same directory match.\n///\n/// Separator hygiene: the filter only *removes* entries, so re-joining the\n/// survivors can never introduce a spurious empty (CWD) entry — no leading,\n/// double, or trailing separator appears that was not already implied by the\n/// input. Existing empty entries already present in `path_var` are preserved\n/// (the \"dir absent → effectively unchanged\" guarantee): an empty entry is not\n/// `dir`, so it survives untouched.\n//\n// Held private by design (a resolve_real_binary-internal helper, like\n// shim_dir): only resolve_real_binary is meant to call it.\nfn strip_dir_from_path(path_var: &str, dir: &std::path::Path) -> String {\n    // `split` on a single separator yields one substring per PATH entry, with\n    // empty entries (leading/double/trailing separators) preserved as \"\" —\n    // which re-join back to the original separator shape. Comparing each entry\n    // as a Path (rather than a raw string) makes `/b` match a `/b/` or\n    // `/x/./b`-style entry without canonicalizing anything on disk.\n    path_var\n        .split(PATH_SEP)\n        .filter(|entry| std::path::Path::new(*entry) != dir)\n        .collect::<Vec<&str>>()\n        .join(PATH_SEP)\n}\n\n/// Find an executable named `name` by walking `path` left to right.\n///\n/// Splits `path` on the OS PATH separator ([`PATH_SEP`]) and, for each entry in\n/// order, checks whether `<entry>/<name>` is an existing executable regular\n/// file. Returns [`Ok`] with the first matching path — PATH order respected —\n/// or [`Err`] naming `name` if no entry matches. A pure lookup over a\n/// caller-supplied PATH string: no environment read of its own and no\n/// `current_exe`. The caller is responsible for stripping gantry's own shim dir\n/// ([`shim_dir`] via [`strip_dir_from_path`]) first, so the lookup cannot\n/// re-resolve `cargo` to the gantry shim itself (plan §1 \"Real-binary\n/// resolution\").\n///\n/// Non-existent entries, directories, and non-executable or non-regular files\n/// are skipped silently: a stale or misconfigured PATH slot is a skip, not a\n/// failure. Reads no environment (no `PATHEXT`) —\n/// the conventional executable extensions are fixed here so this helper honors\n/// the \"no env reads of its own\" contract shared with [`find_in_path`].\n#[cfg(unix)]\nfn is_executable(_candidate: &std::path::Path, md: &std::fs::Metadata) -> bool {\n    use std::os::unix::fs::PermissionsExt;\n    // Any execute bit (user/group/other) qualifies — matching shell PATH\n    // lookup, which treats a file runnable by anyone as found.\n    md.permissions().mode() & 0o111 != 0\n}\n\n#[cfg(windows)]\nfn is_executable(candidate: &std::path::Path, _md: &std::fs::Metadata) -> bool {\n    // No execute bit exists on Windows; runnability is conventionally a\n    // property of the extension. A PATHEXT env read would violate the helper's\n    // \"no env reads of its own\" contract, so the common executable extensions\n    // are matched directly.\n    matches!(\n        candidate.extension().and_then(|e| e.to_str()),\n        Some(\"exe\") | Some(\"bat\") | Some(\"cmd\") | Some(\"com\")\n    )\n}\n\n/// Resolve the real `cargo` binary the shim should hand off to (plan §1\n/// \"Real-binary resolution\", Components §1 \"Shim & dispatcher\").\n///\n/// Composes the three private helpers into the top-level resolution path the\n/// dispatcher consults before any pipeline stage runs:\n///\n/// 1. **Override short-circuit** — when\n///    [`crate::config::Config::real_binary`] is `Some`, return that path\n///    verbatim with *no* PATH search.
